title: Run-and-tumble particles with preferred reorientation
authors: Callum Britton, Ziluo Zhang, Seongjun Han, Thibault Bertrand
abstract: Run-and-tumble particles (RTPs) are canonically modeled with uniform reorientation probabilities, an assumption that breaks down for many biological microswimmers. In this work, we investigate the dynamics of RTPs with arbitrary non-uniform tumble distributions. By deriving an exact Doi-Peliti field theory, we explicitly calculate a wide array of spatial and orientational observables. Notably, we demonstrate that the spatial dynamics exhibit an effective persistence and chirality governed entirely by the first Fourier modes of the tumble distribution, establishing a formal mapping to the dynamics of chiral active Brownian particles. Furthermore, our field-theoretic framework provides a systematic method to compute spatial moments to arbitrary order, allowing for the complete characterization and identification of complex tumbling dynamics. We illustrate the framework with wrapped Gaussian and bimodal Gaussian distributions, demonstrating explicit control over persistence and chirality. We further extend the field theory to $d$ dimensions, recovering the mean squared displacement in terms of a single effective tumble rate. Our results establish a direct link between the shape of the tumble distribution and the emergent dynamics, and provide a foundation for the study of interacting RTPs with non-uniform reorientation.
summary: This work develops an exact Doi-Peliti field theory to analyze run-and-tumble particles with arbitrary, non-uniform reorientation probabilities. By mapping the dynamics onto chiral active Brownian particles, the authors establish a direct quantitative link between the shape of the tumble distribution and emergent transport properties like effective chirality and diffusion. This provides a powerful theoretical framework for studying complex active matter systems.
main_problem: The study investigates the dynamics of run-and-tumble particles (RTPs) when the reorientation (tumble) probabilities are non-uniform, moving beyond the standard uniform assumption.
main_result: The dynamics can be rigorously mapped to those of chiral active Brownian particles (cABPs), and the Mean Squared Displacement (MSD) can be calculated in $d$ dimensions using an effective persistence time ($\Lambda$).
method: The authors derive and utilize an exact Doi-Peliti (DP) field theory formalism, calculating expectation values via path integrals in Fourier space.
model_or_system: The system models active microswimmers (RTPs) whose orientation changes according to a general, non-uniform tumble distribution $\Pi(\psi)$. The dynamics are governed by a Fokker-Planck equation.
key_observables: Mean Squared Displacement (MSD), effective persistence ($\Lambda$), effective chirality ($\Omega$), and higher-order spatial moments.
important_parameters: The first Fourier modes ($\Pi_{\pm 1}$) of the tumble distribution, the tumble rate ($\alpha$), and the spatial dimension ($d$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the DP field theory structure and often assumes non-chiral or specific forms (like von Mises-Fisher) for the tumble distribution to simplify the mapping.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the MSD vs. time for various dimensions ($d=2, 3, 4, 5$) using the von Mises-Fisher distribution, comparing simulation data to analytical results.
paper_structure: The paper develops the DP field theory for general tumble distributions, calculates single-particle observables like MSD, and extends the framework to $d$ dimensions, linking the tumble distribution's Fourier modes to effective particle parameters.
why_interesting: The rigorous field-theoretic approach provides a powerful, systematic tool for characterizing non-equilibrium active matter dynamics, linking microscopic directional biases (tumble shape) to macroscopic transport properties (MSD).
